findings.title: Debug Text Overlay on Title Menu
findings.where: Title screen, above the 'New Driver' menu button
findings.problem: An unprompted debug-style text block ($9 | 2030-01-01 (DAY) – smduel) is placed over the primary menu
findings.why: Makes the game look unfinished and confuses players about whether the text is part of intended UI or a glitch
findings.fix: Permanently remove the debug text line from the title screen’s menu area

findings.title: Static Radar Without Functional Cues
findings.where: Arena and road screens, bottom-left radar panel
findings.problem: The radar is a static green circle with no sweep animation, contact markers, or active feedback
findings.why: Players cannot distinguish between a non-functional radar and an idle one, eroding trust in UI instrumentation
findings.fix: Add a slow-moving (1 rotation every 3 seconds) green sweep line from the radar’s center to signal active scanning

findings.title: Subtle Building Interactivity Markers
findings.where: City screen, small yellow icons adjacent to buildings
findings.problem: Tiny yellow markers fail to contrast against the cracked gray terrain and lack visual weight
findings.why: Players struggle to identify interactive buildings, slowing progression and increasing frustration with exploration
findings.fix: Enlarge the yellow markers by 50% and add a thin white outline to boost contrast against the gray terrain

findings.title: Non-Interactive Weapon Row Cues
findings.problem: Empty weapon rows only display '(empty)' with no visual indication of selectability
findings.why: Players miss the prompt to press Enter to mount weapons, causing confusion during vehicle setup
findings.fix: Replace '(empty)' with 'Press Enter to Mount' and add a faint cyan outline to rows when hovered by the cursor

findings.title: Ambiguous Body Armor Status Indicator
findings.where: Arena and road screens, right-side CONDITION panel (Body armor line)
findings.problem: A red 'x' next to body armor (0/3) lacks explicit visual context for its meaning
findings.why: Players cannot quickly determine if the 'x' signifies missing, broken, or unequipped armor, harming real-time status readability
findings.fix: Replace the red 'x' with a red broken shield icon to explicitly indicate non-functional or missing body armor
